title: Chicken or Turkey Salad with Egg

content.title: About
content.content: Chicken or turkey salad with egg is a light dish featuring boiled poultry, hard‑boiled eggs, fresh vegetables, and a light dressing. It is popular both at home and in cafeterias thanks to its high protein content and satisfying flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Chicken and turkey are among the most widely consumed meats worldwide.
The egg adds not only taste but also important nutrients such as vitamin D and choline.
Traditional recipes often include celery, carrot, and green onion for extra crunch.
The salad can be prepared in advance, but the dressing is best added just before serving to keep vegetables fresh.
In some countries the salad is served with a mustard or yogurt‑based dressing.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Chicken, turkey and eggs provide high‑quality complete protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Low in carbohydrates
items.content: The salad contains virtually no carbs, making it suitable for low‑carb diets.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: Poultry and eggs supply B6, B12 and niacin, supporting energy metabolism.

items.title: Contains minerals
items.content: Iron, zinc and phosphorus in the salad contribute to blood health and bone strength.

items.title: Promotes satiety
items.content: High protein and moderate fat content help keep you feeling full longer.

items.title: Egg allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to eggs, ranging from skin rashes to anaphylaxis.

items.title: Bacterial contamination risk
items.content: Undercooked poultry or eggs can harbor salmonella; ensure all ingredients are fully cooked.

items.title: High sodium in dressing
items.content: Store‑bought dressings may contain a lot of salt, which should be limited for people with hypertension.

items.title: Dietary restrictions
items.content: Those following vegetarian or vegan diets should replace meat and eggs with plant‑based alternatives.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the salad chilled as a main dish or as a side to soups. It can be eaten with a fork or spoon, or used as a filling for wraps or whole‑grain bread.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the prepared salad in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days. If the dressing is stored separately, combine it just before serving to maintain vegetable crunch.
